children: OTTAWA--Canada's Finance Minister has ordered the country's tax-collection agency to prioritize rulings for investors about the tax treatment on proposed large transactions.

François-Philippe Champagne, who is also responsible for the Canada Revenue Agency, said the need for accelerated decisions will give major investors "the clarity and certainty they need" to strike deals in this country.

The order was issued Monday, at the start of an investment summit Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is hosting, in which officials are trying to match deep-pocketed global investors with domestic firms seeking cash for their shovel-ready projects. One of Carney's policy priorities is to accelerate the construction of trade corridors and resource projects to build up resilience in an economy weakened by Trump administration tariffs.
A recent Canadian government audit indicated that most tax rulings are issued within 90 days. Champagne's statement didn't quantify how quickly the decisions will now emerge under this new directive.

Tax officials are now expected to expedite advanced income-tax rulings related to investments of 1 billion Canadian dollars (US$721 million) and above. These rulings provide certainty with respect to how Canada's tax laws will apply to certain transactions, according to a note published by Toronto law firm Rosen & Associates.
